Article Title: Google DeepMind launches Genie 4, CEO Sundar Pichai calls it ‘our most realistic and interactive world model’
Article Text:
Excited to share Genie 4 today our most realistic and interactive world model:

- steer dynamic environments in real time, shaping events, camera angles, and actions

- generate native audio matched to the world, from realistic background sounds to characters who can converse in real time!

- simulate photorealistic scenes and real-world physics

- create more coherent multi-step events through reasoning from Gemini

We've started to roll out as a research preview to trusted testers.

Coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners via the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Genie 4 is built on Gemini Intelligence

Google lists four core breakthroughs in Genie 4

Real-time scene direction

Advanced physics and motion

Native audio generation

Complex multi-step simulation

Google DeepMind has officially unveiled Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model that introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. The system allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly while the model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes. Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the milestone, calling Genie 4 “our most realistic and interactive world model.”Genie 4 is not a standalone graphics engine; it directly integrates the multimodal reasoning capabilities of Google’s Gemini family:Gemini Omni: Anchors each simulation in authentic real-world appearances, physical dynamics and visual continuity.Gemini reasoning models: Maintain scene logic, ensuring events unfold with cause-and-effect coherence over time.Gemini 3.8 Flash: Operates as an active agent in the loop. As Genie 4 renders the world, Gemini 3.8 Flash tracks incoming frames, breaks broad goals into sequential steps, verifies that actions succeed, and adapts plans instantly whenever the scene shifts or a user intervenes.Google DeepMind detailed four primary technical advancements that define the new world model:Users can explore simulated environments using standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera positioning, while using plain text prompts to alter the world in real time. They can change the weather, adjust camera angles, or introduce new characters and objects.Google says that Genie 4 delivers a significant leap in physical accuracy, accurately rendering complex interactions such as aerodynamics, collisions, and environmental resistance. Character animation sees an equally sharp upgrade: digital figures move naturally, interact organically with their surroundings, and respond immediately to real-time steering.As the first real-time world model to generate synchronised audio natively, Genie 4 produces sound directly alongside visual frames, Google says. This includes contextual ambient soundscapes, such as wind through trees or breaking ocean waves as well as background music.Crucially, the model handles interactive, real-time spoken dialogue. Characters converse, react, and respond on the fly to user prompts and unfolding environmental events.By pairing world generation with advanced AI reasoning, Genie 4 can simulate multi-stage events, allowing developers to see how artificial agents navigate complex settings before deploying them into real-world scenarios.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model. System introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. System allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly. Model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes.

Article Title: Scale AI’s Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers; a privacy group alleges up to 19 trackers monitor workers and is asking European regulators to fine the company
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

What do the complaints allege about worker tracking

“You don't work when you want,

“You work when the platform wants you to and there are tasks available.”

Why are Scale AI’s identity checks being challenged

Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria against the company founded by Meta’s current chief AI officer and highest-paid employee, Alexandr Wang. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models. According to the Reuters report, the complaints say up to 19 trackers monitor workers, including by recording keystrokes and mouse movements every few seconds.Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers performing tasks for clients such as Meta, OpenAI and Google. Noyb is asking European regulators to fine Scale AI and examine how the platform assigns work. The complaints also challenge its identity checks and how it handles workers’ requests for their personal data.The complaints, which Reuters reviewed, describe monitoring that records workers’ activity throughout their tasks. An investigation by Paris-based research collective DiPLab found that the resulting data file could be reconstructed into a video replaying a work session from beginning to end.Thomas Le Bonniec, who spent two years studying Outlier for DiPLab, also questioned how much control freelancers have over their schedules.” Le Bonniec said.Noyb’s request that regulators examine task allocation raises concerns about how the platform decides which work is available to freelancers.Workers must submit identification documents and a facial video to Persona, an identity verification company. The complaints allege that these checks were invasive, repeated without explanation, and breached European Union rules governing biometric data, which can identify people through physical characteristics. However, these are mere allegations in the complaints, not findings announced by regulators.DiPLab’s investigation also identified game-like mechanisms that encouraged workers to complete tasks, with bonuses as a key part of the incentive system. Citing worker interviews, Le Bonniec said Outlier offered bonuses of $100 to $200 for completing 200 tasks within 24 hours.He pointed to a 2021 fine Italy’s data protection authority imposed on delivery platform Glovo for similar gamification practices, in which rewards or targets are used to influence workers’ behaviour.Separately, four workers requested copies of their personal data from Outlier between December 2025 and May 2026. According to the complaints, none received an answer.
Article Summary: Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints against the company. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models.

Article Title: Ohio is asking voters to report screenshots when ChatGPT, Claude or Grok gives incorrect election information, launching the effort a week before the midterms while its own AI assistant serves 88 coun
Article Text:
Ohio is asking voters to report screenshots when ChatGPT, Claude or Grok gives incorrect election information (AI-generated image)

Here’s what Ohio Secretary of State said

"Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose announced an ongoing effort today to help ensure voters receive accurate election information when using artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and other generative AI chatbots.

The office’s cybersecurity and technology teams are also working to ensure public information on the Secretary of State’s website is accessible to AI platforms while maintaining rigorous cybersecurity standards. For months, the office engaged with private-sector partners and AI companies to identify inaccurate information and improve how authoritative Ohio election information is provided to users.

“As more people turn to AI for everyday information, we need to make sure Ohio’s voters know where the facts come from,” said Secretary LaRose.

“AI can be an incredibly useful tool, but when it comes to elections, voters should always verify what they see with an official source.”

The initiative builds on Ohio’s responsible use of AI in election administration. Last year, the Secretary of State’s office developed EVA, the Election Virtual Assistant, to help Ohio’s 88 county boards of elections quickly access accurate information grounded in the Election Official Manual and official election calendar.

Ohioans using AI for election information should follow a few simple best practices:

Check the source. Information should be supported by official sources such as VoteOhio.gov, the Secretary of State’s office or a county board of elections.

Verify before acting. Confirm voting dates, hours, polling locations, identification requirements and deadlines with an official election source.

Be cautious of unsourced answers. AI-generated information can be incorrect or outdated, even when presented confidently.

Ohioans can also help identify problems. Anyone who receives false or misleading Ohio election information from an AI platform is encouraged to send the Secretary of State’s office screenshots showing the prompt, complete response and AI platform used.

Reports can be sent by direct message to @VerifyOhio on X, Facebook or Instagram, or by email to helpmeout@ohiosos.gov. The office will use these reports to identify recurring inaccuracies and work with technology partners to improve the information reaching voters.

“AI is changing how people find information, and government needs to keep pace,” said LaRose. “Ohio is embracing innovation responsibly while making sure voters know that official election sources remain the gold standard.”

Ohio has asked its voters to report screenshots when AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok provide incorrect or misleading election information. Announced by Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose via an official press release, the initiative comes a week before the midterm elections and aims to help identify inaccurate answers and improve how AI platforms share official voting information. Voters can send screenshots of the prompt, the full response and the platform used to the Secretary of State’s office. “The office’s cybersecurity and technology teams are also working to ensure public information on the Secretary of State’s website is accessible to AI platforms while maintaining rigorous cybersecurity standards”, the release said.The effort builds on Ohio’s use of its own AI assistant, the Election Virtual Assistant (EVA), which helps all 88 county boards of elections access information based on the state’s Election Official Manual and official election calendar. In the release, LaRose urged voters to verify details such as polling locations, voting hours and deadlines through official sources before acting on AI-generated answers.
Article Summary: Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose announced an ongoing effort today to help ensure voters receive accurate election information when using artificial intelligence platforms. Voters can send screenshots of the prompt, the full response and the platform used to the Secretary of state’s office.

Article Title: Our priority is to build FFI into a lasting part of the country’s gaming community: Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena
Article Text:
Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena

Garena already has Free Fire Max as one of the most popular mobile action games in India. How does Free Fire India make a difference to users in India?

How is Garena balancing an engaging player experience with measures that encourage healthy gaming habits, particularly among younger audiences?

Data security and regulatory compliance have become important considerations for digital platforms in India. How have these considerations shaped Garena's approach to developing and operating Free Fire India?

As competitive gaming continues to grow in India, how does Garena see the role of grassroots and collegiate competitions in developing Indian esports talent and creating opportunities to compete internationally?

Looking ahead, what are Garena's priorities for Free Fire India, and how does the company envision strengthening its engagement with India's gaming community, including players, creators and esports talent?

Garena has announced the availability of Free Fire India (FFI) starting October 28. Available as a standalone app on the App Store and Google Play, FFI, according to the company, will offer exciting gameplay, opportunities to connect with friends and locally relevant content. On Free Fire India's launch, Times of India spoke to Vaibhav Das Mundhra, head of operations, India, Garena on the game and the company's India plans.Free Fire India (FFI) is a new standalone app developed specifically for mobile gamers in India, offering fast-paced gameplay, an engaging social experience and broad device accessibility. We have optimised FFI to run smoothly on a wide range of smartphones, including lower-specification devices, making the game accessible to more players across India. Free Fire MAX will remain as a separate app for players using higher-specification devices. For us, bringing FFI to players is also a way to build on our relationship with India’s gaming community over the years. As part of this, we will be introducing an in-game Diwali campaign, featuring localised bundles.We have built several safeguards into FFI to support responsible gameplay and help players maintain a healthy balance. These include age-verification features, with users under 18 needing consent from a parent or guardian before creating an account, regular break reminders, and defined playtime limits, which is up to 6 hours per day for users above 18 and up to 3 hours for users under 18. Spending caps will apply to users under 18, while in-game purchases remain optional. Some visual effects have also been modified, with red blood and certain other effects removed or replaced.We are committed to promoting responsible gameplay and fostering positive community engagement. Through “Play It Right”, we devote significant resources to helping FFI players develop healthy gaming habits and contribute to a supportive gaming community. The initiative focuses on developing educational and short-video content, relatable comics, break reminder notifications breaks, limiting playtime, and focusing on their overall well-being. These safeguards are part of how we are building a more responsible environment for players and families, while allowing the community to enjoy the game in a healthy and balanced way.When we prepared FFI for availability in India, data protection and local requirements were important considerations for us. The game will be hosted on servers in India, and sensitive personal data of Indian users related to FFI will be stored locally in India. We have also taken feedback from relevant government authorities into account as we prepared the game for players here. Our focus is on protecting player data and operating in line with applicable Indian laws and regulations.In developing and operating FFI, we also draw on Garena’s development expertise across markets, with a local team in India supporting the game’s marketing and operations.We believe grassroots and collegiate competitions play an important role in nurturing Indian esports talent. These tournaments provide aspiring players and teams with opportunities to hone their skills, gain competitive experience, and progress through different levels of competition.Our priority is to build FFI into a lasting part of the country’s gaming community. This starts with delivering a familiar, engaging experience tailored to players in India, while encouraging safe and responsible play. We will continue developing the game in ways that give players more opportunities to enjoy themselves and connect with one another.We are grateful for the support players, creators, and competitive gaming communities have shown us over the years, and hope to continue building on these relationships. Our local team will support marketing and operations, helping us stay attuned to the needs and interests of the community. We will also continue to explore in-game campaigns that celebrate India's diverse cultures and communities.We see this as a long-term effort, and look forward to sharing more about future initiatives as they take shape.
Article Summary: Free Fire India (FFI) is a new standalone app developed specifically for mobile gamers in India. Available as a standalone app on the App Store and Google Play, FFI, according to the company, will offer exciting gameplay, opportunities to connect with friends and locally relevant content.

Article Title: Dyson study finds 1 in 2 Indians frequently miss cleaning under beds and furniture
Article Text: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning, according to Dyson's first 'How India Cleans' study. The survey also found that hair left behind on floors and dust quickly resettling after cleaning remain among the biggest frustrations for consumers. The study, conducted among over 650 respondents across seven Indian cities, examines how Indians clean their homes, the challenges they face and what they expect from modern floorcare technology. According to the findings, 52% of respondents said spaces beneath beds and furniture are frequently missed during cleaning, while 48% reported difficulties cleaning corners, edges and skirting areas.Despite significant time spent on household cleaning, many consumers continue to struggle with achieving a thorough clean. Dyson said more than half of respondents spend between 30 minutes and an hour cleaning floors, while another 11% spend up to two hours.The study highlights that the issue is not just how often people clean, but whether existing cleaning tools can effectively tackle different surfaces and hard-to-reach spaces throughout the home.According to the survey, 36% of respondents identified human or pet hair left behind on floors as one of their biggest cleaning pain points. Meanwhile, 38% said dust settles again quickly after cleaning, creating the impression that surfaces become dirty soon after they have been cleaned. Dyson noted that household dust can easily become airborne due to everyday activity before resettling on surfaces, making effective dust removal a continuing challenge.The study found that Indian households often feature a mix of flooring types that require different cleaning approaches. While hard flooring remains common, 72% of respondents said they also have carpets and rugs at home. Other common surfaces include marble (51%), vitrified or ceramic tiles (49%), and granite (43%). This diversity means consumers increasingly seek cleaning solutions that can move seamlessly across different floor types without compromising performance.When selecting floorcare products, respondents indicated a strong preference for advanced technology. Around 61% said better technology influenced their purchase decisions, ahead of cleaning performance (54%) and brand trust (49%). In comparison, only 21% cited pricing and promotional offers as a key factor. The survey also found that vacuum cleaners are increasingly being used for whole-home cleaning rather than just floor maintenance. Respondents reported using them under furniture (71%), on hard floors (70%), carpets and rugs (69%), upholstery (69%), and beds and mattresses (63%).Commenting on the findings, Tim Hare, Design and Development Engineer, Floor Care at Dyson, said consumers increasingly expect vacuum cleaners to tackle multiple cleaning challenges in a single session, ranging from fine dust and long hair to different floor surfaces and hard-to-reach areas. The company said insights from the study help shape the development of future floorcare products by identifying real-world cleaning problems and unmet consumer needs.Alongside the study, Dyson highlighted its recently launched Dyson V16 Piston Animal cordless vacuum cleaner, priced at ₹79,900. The company said the device is designed to address common household cleaning challenges through features such as automatic floor-type sensing, anti-tangle technology for long hair, LED illumination for spotting hidden dust, and up to 70 minutes of fade-free suction.The appliance also includes Dyson's CleanCompaktor bin technology, which the company claims can compress dust and debris to increase storage capacity and reduce the frequency of emptying. The findings underscore a growing consumer focus on cleaning effectiveness rather than just effort, with many households seeking technology-driven solutions that can deliver a more complete clean across modern homes.
Article Summary: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning. The survey also found that hair left behind on floors and dust quickly resettling after cleaning remain among the biggest frustrations for consumers. The study was conducted among over 650 respondents across seven Indian cities.

Elon Musk has a 'failure warning' for these technology companies; says: Investors have already started betting against them

What are neoclouds

“As someone with a portfolio of energized land assets here is what I am seeing:

1. Neoclouds are disorganized and poorly capitalized. Some are definitely better than others however.

2. Hyperscalers are intractable, bureaucratic organizations that take 3 months to do an NDA and want 18mo escrow periods. We built our portfolio by competing against these terms because of our speed and simplicity.

The more future assets orgs like ours win, the bigger the problem for the hyperscalers downstream (see 3).

3. There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027. Hyperacalers will (obviously) react by focusing on their own internal compute needs over any third party. If the third party is a model company, they will tell them to go through their model router where they will also take a non-trivial vig.

Them telling Ant they have no compute for them (rumored in Ant’s S-1) if true is a huge tell that this is already happening.

All of this is to say that it does look like there will be a lot of partially stranded compute and compute sitting in inventory in 2027 than is currently forecasted. This is bought and paid for but effectively underearning (below total cost of capital) or collecting dust. We see this as true for everyone - model companies, hyperscalers, neoclouds except ONE (you can guess which one).

This dislocation will benefit two kinds of orgs: the non-bureaucratic big scalers who can build industrial scale quickly and the nimble, well capitalized players feeding them.

2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. It will also be a consolidation year for a few.”
Article Summary: 2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. The more future assets orgs like ours win, the bigger the problem for the hyperscalers downstream. There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027.

Article Title: Apple releases macOS 27.2 Golden Gate: Features, how to download and more
Article Text:
Apple releases macOS 27.2 Golden Gate

How to download macOS 27.2 Golden Gate

Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner of your screen.

Open System Settings.

Click General and select Software Update.

Wait for your MacBook to check for available updates.

If macOS 27.2 Golden Gate is available for your device, click Upgrade Now or Update Now.

Enter your administrator password if prompted and follow the on-screen instructions to complete the installation.

macOS 27 Golden Gate features

A rebuilt search index for Spotlight, Photos and Mail

Apple has released latest macOS 27.2 Golden Gate software, marking the first major update to macOS 27 since its launch in September this year. Among other changes, the update brings changes to brightness and volume sliders. It also expands Siri AI to new languages including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. In its release notes, Apple said: “This update provides enhancements to Siri AI with the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions as well as draw from a wider range of personal context. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your Mac”.To download the macOS 27.2 Golden Gate on your MacBook, follow the steps below:First announced at WWDC in June this year, the macOS 27 Golden Gate software update features a transparency slider that runs from completely clear to fully tinted, so you pick your poison. Sidebars stretch to the edge of the window with refraction continuing underneath them, sidebar icons keep their colour, and every window shares the same corner radius—even apps that haven't been updated.App icons pick up extra Liquid Glass layers built directly into the artwork.The plumbing behind Spotlight, Photos and Mail has been rearchitected. New stuff gets indexed almost immediately rather than disappearing into the void for hours, and a full reindex runs once after you update. Should fix the "why can't Finder find this file I made twenty minutes ago" problem that's dogged Tahoe.Siri AI lands on the Mac too—the Gemini-collaborated version, with onscreen awareness, personal context, and its own app. It's wired into Spotlight, so you can summon it from the same place you'd hunt for a file. Right-click on any window or item to ask Siri about it directly, or select multiple files in Finder and have it compare them for you. Conversation history syncs across devices via iCloud, so a thread you start on the Mac picks up on the iPhone or Watch.
Article Summary: macOS 27.2 Golden Gate features a rebuilt search index for Spotlight, Photos and Mail. Gemini-collaborated version of Siri adds onscreen awareness, personal context, and its own app. Sidebars stretch to the edge of the window with refraction continuing underneath them.

Article Title: Apple launches new iPad mini with bigger OLED screen and A20 Pro chip: Price in India, features and more
Article Text:
The new iPad mini starts at Rs 82,900 in India

A20 Pro makes the iPad mini much faster at AI and gaming

iPad mini price in India now starts at Rs 82,900

Two years after a quiet chip bump, the iPad mini is back with a proper redesign. The new iPad mini moves to an 8.5-inch OLED display, up from 8.3 inches, and pairs it with the A20 Pro chip, IP67 water and dust resistance, and a 5.4mm body that is thinner and lighter than before. Pre-orders open in India on October 28, with sales starting November 6.The timing stands out. Apple announced the tablet two days before its "Pro and tell" event on Wednesday, giving the smallest iPad a spotlight of its own. It is also the first proper redesign since 2021, after the 2024 model arrived as mostly a chip and storage refresh.The footprint stays the same despite the bigger screen, thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner. Peak brightness climbs to 1,200 nits, more than double the previous model, and the display can dim to just 1 nit for late-night reading. A nano-texture glass option, until now limited to the iPad Pro, is also available to cut glare outdoors.Built on a 2nm process, the A20 Pro has a 6-core CPU and a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in every core. Apple claims up to 4.5x faster AI performance, 2.7x faster graphics and 60% quicker multithreaded performance over the last generation.The 512GB variant adds a Dual 16-core Neural Engine for heavier on-device AI tasks like running local language models.The iPad mini also supports Siri AI, arriving in beta with iPadOS 27.2. The 12MP Center Stage front camera moves to the landscape edge, fixing the off-centre framing on video calls. Apple's N1 chip adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and cellular models get the C2 modem with up to 50% faster data speeds. A new Acoustic Display routes bass through the screen for fuller sound.The Wi-Fi model costs Rs 82,900, while the Wi-Fi + Cellular version is priced at Rs 1,00,900. Students can get it from Rs 76,900 with education pricing. The 2024 iPad mini went on sale at Rs 49,900, before a price hike earlier this year took it to Rs 69,900.The tablet comes in midnight and starlight, with 128GB, 256GB and 512GB storage options. The new TechWoven Smart Folio costs Rs 8,500, and both the Apple Pencil Pro (Rs 11,900) and Apple Pencil USB-C (Rs 7,900) are supported.
Article Summary: The new iPad mini moves to an 8.5-inch OLED display, up from 8.3 inches. It pairs it with the A20 Pro chip, IP67 water and dust resistance, and a 5.4mm body that is thinner and lighter than before. Apple announced the tablet two days before its "Pro and tell" event.

Article Title: Dell expands AI factory with NVIDIA, announces new agentic AI solutions and infrastructure
Article Text: Dell Technologies has unveiled a broad set of updates to its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, introducing new agentic AI solutions, deskside AI offerings, validated ecosystem integrations and purpose-built infrastructure aimed at helping enterprises move AI projects from experimentation to production. The company said more than 6,500 customers have now adopted the platform, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter.The announcement comes as enterprises increasingly look to deploy agentic AI systems that can reason, make decisions and perform tasks autonomously. Dell said the latest expansion of its AI portfolio is designed to provide organisations with greater control over their AI infrastructure, data, models and operations while addressing concerns around costs, governance and return on investment.According to the company, the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA combines infrastructure, software, ecosystem partnerships and managed services to help businesses deploy AI workloads on infrastructure they own and control. The company argued that enterprises are prioritising end-to-end AI lifecycle support and are seeking alternatives to cloud-only deployments.As part of the update, Dell announced that Reflection's Beam open-weight model has been validated on the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA, giving enterprises access to an Apache 2.0-licensed model designed for software engineering and long-horizon agentic AI workloads.Dell also expanded its AI ecosystem through integrations with partners including Dynatrace for AI observability, Mistral for knowledge assistants and agentic AI platforms, and Fogsphere for computer vision applications. The company said the ecosystem now spans AI models, applications and operating systems, including support for SUSE Linux.The company additionally highlighted a multilayered security architecture that combines hardware-rooted infrastructure, NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture and Red Hat AI Factory software to help enterprises securely deploy autonomous AI agents at scale.Dell also expanded its Dell Deskside Agentic AI portfolio with new validated deployment templates designed to help businesses scale AI workloads from a single developer workstation to deployments of more than 1,000 systems. The new solutions include blueprints for agentic coding, AI-powered workflows, NVIDIA NemoClaw deployments, Hermes Agent implementations and higher-education AI lab environments.On the hardware front, Dell announced a new 64GB unified-memory configuration of the Dell Pro Precision with GB10, aimed at developers and smaller teams working on local AI development projects. The company said systems can be clustered together to support larger AI models and more complex workflows. Dell also disclosed that the Dell Pro Precision with GB300 workstation will soon be available with Windows support, delivering up to 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of FP4 compute performance.To support growing AI workloads, Dell introduced several new infrastructure offerings.Among them is the Dell Modular Data Center with NVIDIA DSX POD, a containerised, factory-integrated AI infrastructure design that includes compute, storage, networking, power and liquid cooling systems aimed at accelerating AI deployments.The company also announced the Dell PowerEdge M9882, a server platform featuring 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs in a single rack designed for agent orchestration, code execution and other AI execution workloads. For mainstream enterprise environments, Dell introduced the Dell PowerEdge R8822, an air-cooled server optimised for agentic AI workloads, data processing, analytics and reinforcement learning.Another addition is the Dell PowerEdge XE9810, which Dell said will provide rack-scale inference capabilities using Groq 3 Language Processing Units for high-throughput production AI deployments. The company also unveiled new NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platforms running on Dell PowerEdge servers, targeting telecom operators that want to run radio access network and AI workloads on a shared infrastructure.
Article Summary: More than 6,500 customers have now adopted the platform, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter. Dell said the latest expansion of its AI portfolio is designed to provide organisations with greater control over their AI infrastructure, data, models and operations.

Article Title: Apple Pro and tell event: Touchscreen MacBook Pro, M6 iMac, OLED iPad mini and more expected
Article Text:
Apple is expected to unveil its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at the Pro and tell event on October 28.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro brings OLED and the Dynamic Island to the Mac

M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are expected after a two-year wait

Apple's Pro and tell event takes place in Los Angeles this Wednesday, October 28, at 10am Pacific time, or 10:30pm IST. The company hasn't confirmed what it will show, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects a busy day of Mac and iPad news. Headlining the list is Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro. It will be joined by an M6 version of the entry-level MacBook Pro, an M6 iMac and an iPad mini with an OLED display.Marketing chief Greg Joswiak teased the announcements on October 19 with a short "Can't wait to pro and tell next week" post. This is Apple's second event this month. It comes two weeks after the Welcome Home showcase in New York, where the company introduced the HomeView smart display, the HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K.Writing in his Power On newsletter, Gurman says the higher-end MacBook Pro will come in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with an OLED touchscreen, a first on both counts for the Mac. The laptop looks similar to current models but weighs less, adds the iPhone's Dynamic Island and runs on M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. It is also expected to cost significantly more than today's top MacBook Pros.Touch will be an extra option, with the keyboard and trackpad staying central.Apple is tweaking macOS Golden Gate so that it presents controls based on whether someone has been tapping the screen or using the trackpad. Tapping a button can bring up a menu around the finger, and the Dock and Menu Bar have been reworked for touch. Gurman has said on his podcast that the laptop could go on sale on November 6.It is quite a reversal for a company whose co-founder Steve Jobs called touchscreen laptops "ergonomically terrible" back in 2010.The regular 14-inch MacBook Pro will keep its current design but move from the M5 to the M6 chip, which arrived with the Mac mini in August. Reports suggest it could pick up a hole-punch camera, along with a price increase as component shortages ripple across Apple's lineup. Gurman says a redesigned version of this model is planned for next year.The iMac is set to jump straight from the M4 to the M6, nearly two years after its last refresh. Little else is expected to change, though new colour options are possible.The iPad mini, meanwhile, could become the first iPad outside the Pro line to switch to OLED. It is expected to move to the A20 chip from the iPhone 18, and the new screen may push its price up.Apple's Mac lineup will be crowded after Wednesday, stretching from the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air to three kinds of MacBook Pro. Gurman says OLED versions of the MacBook Air and iMac are already in testing, though neither is imminent. A refreshed non-OLED MacBook Air is due early next year.
Article Summary: M6 iMac and OLED iPad mini are expected after a two-year wait. Apple's Pro and tell event takes place in Los Angeles this Wednesday, October 28, at 10am Pacific time, or 10:30pm IST. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects a busy day of Mac and iPad news.

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
